name: Dawn at the harbour
synopsis: A small fishing harbour at daybreak. An old fisherman readies his trawler, casts off and heads for the open sea while the light turns from blue to gold.
direction.univers: A small Breton fishing harbour at daybreak, calm and down to earth. The film follows an old trawler as it leaves, with no dialogue.
direction.personnages: A fisherman in his sixties, faded yellow oilskin, short grey beard, weathered hands. No other character.
direction.photographie: 35 mm lens, locked-off camera or very slow tracking shots, eye level, natural depth of field, no handheld camera.
direction.palette: Low dawn light, cold blues turning to gold, light mist on the water, no neon and no text in the frame.
direction.rythme: Five-second shots, cuts on the movement of the water, a slow build toward the open sea, no abrupt movement.
shot.1.label: The sleeping harbour
shot.1.prompt: Wide shot of a small fishing harbour at dawn, moored trawlers, light mist on the calm water, cold blue light, static camera, no people.
shot.2.label: The fisherman’s hands
shot.2.prompt: Close-up of the hands of an old fisherman in a faded yellow oilskin coiling a wet rope on the deck, low golden light, very slow dolly in.
shot.3.label: The departure
shot.3.prompt: An old trawler slowly leaves the quay, wake on the calm water, slow pan from the jetty, mist lifting, golden light.
shot.4.label: The gulls
shot.4.prompt: Gulls circling above the water against the light, sun rising through the mist, medium shot, slow and fluid movement.
shot.5.label: Out to sea
shot.5.prompt: Very wide shot, the tiny trawler facing the rising sun, sky turning from blue to gold, static camera, light mist.
